\]

- On the sphere, \(r=a\), so \(\mathbf{F} = k a^n \hat{\mathbf{r}}\).
- The outward unit normal \(\hat{\mathbf{n}}\) on a sphere is \(\hat{\mathbf{r}}\).
- The surface element is \(ds = a^2 \sin\theta\, d\theta\, d\phi\).

(a) \(\displaystyle \iint_S \mathbf{F}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}\,ds\):

\[
\mathbf{F}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}} = (k a^n \hat{\mathbf{r}})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{r}} = k a^n
\]

\iint_S \mathbf{F}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}\,ds 
= k a^n \iint_S ds 
= k a^n (4\pi a^2)
= 4\pi k\, a^{n+2}
\]

(b) \(\displaystyle \iint_S \mathbf{F}\times\hat{\mathbf{n}}\,ds\):

\[
\mathbf{F}\times\hat{\mathbf{n}} = (k a^n \hat{\mathbf{r}})\times\hat{\mathbf{r}} = 0
\]
Hence
\[
\iint_S \mathbf{F}\times\hat{\mathbf{n}}\,ds = \mathbf{0}
\]

- Any purely radial field of the form \(k r^n\hat{\mathbf{r}}\) has zero tangential component on a sphere, so the net “circulation-type” surface integral involving \(\mathbf{F}\times\hat{\mathbf{n}}\) over the closed spherical surface is zero.

\boxed{\iint_S \mathbf{F}\times\hat{\mathbf{n}}\,ds = \mathbf{0}}
\]
